newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Editorials - July 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Editorials - July 3.

text.p: These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- APPLE DAILY said Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa did not talk much about democracy and human rights in his inauguration speech, neither were elections for the first Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR) legislature included. The paper said making Hong Kong less political did not mean the government had to suppress democracy. By forbidding people to voice their opinions, the new government could only make Hong Kong more politcised, not less, it said.

-- The Beijing-backed TA KUNG PAO said the "one country, two systems" policy would bring new opportunities and challenges to the territory. The paper called on Hong Kong people to try to get to know China, love the motherland and support the work of the SAR government.

-- The English-language HONGKONG STANDARD said Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa could be expected to be active and assertive in guiding and influencing the economy. But in view of Tung's conservative nature, people were more likely to see a series of fine adjustments and a process of gradual evolution, rather than any radical departures in policy.
